title: Defence Evaluation and Research Agency → QinetiQ
summary: The Defence Evaluation and Research Agency (DERA), created on 1 April 1995 by amalgamating Ministry of Defence research establishments, was split on 1 July 2001: the larger part, including most non-nuclear test and evaluation sites, became QinetiQ, while work kept inside government went to the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl). The MoD sold a stake to the Carlyle Group (announced December 2002), then floated QinetiQ on the London Stock Exchange in February 2006. The National Audit Office reported in 2007 net proceeds of £576 million to date, with the MoD keeping a 19 per cent stake, and concluded the taxpayer could have received more.

private.name: QinetiQ (QinetiQ Group plc)
funders: The Carlyle Group (minority investor from 2002–03 until the 2006 flotation)
private.outcome: QinetiQ was floated on the London Stock Exchange on 10 February 2006 at 200p a share, the top of its range, in an offering The Register described as a £1.3bn IPO. The NAO reported in November 2007 that the MoD had received net proceeds of £576 million and still held a 19 per cent stake.

links.claim: On 1 July 2001 the MoD split DERA into QinetiQ and Dstl. The National Archives records that the commercialised part of DERA was re-created as the QinetiQ Group; QinetiQ says it took the larger part, including most of the non-nuclear testing and evaluation sites.

links.claim: In December 2002 the MoD announced the sale of a stake in QinetiQ to the Carlyle Group: Carlyle would acquire a 33.8% economic interest, 3.7% would go to employees, and the MoD would keep 62.5%, planning to sell its whole stake within 3-5 years, probably by flotation. The NAO later reported the MoD received £155 million for the 37.5% stake.

sources.title: Sale of a Stake in QinetiQ PLC to The Carlyle Group

links.claim: QinetiQ shares began trading on the London Stock Exchange on 10 February 2006 at 200p; the NAO reported that the privatisation had produced net proceeds of £576 million to date and that the MoD still held a 19 per cent stake.
After privatisation QinetiQ held a Long Term Partnering Agreement with the MoD that The Register, reporting on the NAO study, said could be worth up to £5.6bn to QinetiQ through 2028.

sources.title: Watchdog raps MoD over Qinetiq sell-off bonanza

claims.claim: Taxpayers were short-changed in the privatisation of QinetiQ while Carlyle and managers profited.
claims.explanation: The NAO found the process well managed and the 2006 flotation well executed, but believed the taxpayer could have received more money from the deal; it found the top ten managers' shares were worth £107 million at flotation from an investment of just over £500,000. The Register reported Carlyle made about £300m profit on a £42m investment, a press figure rather than an audited one.
